blocks.title: Floor-level controlled Achilles lowering
coaching_cues: Beside stable support on firm level ground, raise both heels, then transfer weight to the affected leg and slowly lower its heel only to the floor. Do not use a step, lower into deep dorsiflexion, increase depth or add speed or weight. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.
blocks.instructions: Beside stable support on firm level ground, raise both heels, then transfer weight to the affected leg and slowly lower its heel only to the floor. Do not use a step, lower into deep dorsiflexion, increase depth or add speed or weight. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.
stop_rules: Once daily only: 1 set of 10 controlled lowerings beside stable support on level ground.
Bodyweight only: no added resistance.
No step or lowering below floor level.
No speed, bouncing, hopping or automatic progression.
Stop for worsening during or delayed symptoms and seek clinical review.
Stop and seek assessment for a snap, sudden pain or loss of function.
Follow clinician restrictions; this prescription grants no training or contact clearance.

drill_snapshot.name: Floor-level controlled Achilles lowering
drill_snapshot.notes: Beside stable support on firm level ground, raise both heels, then transfer weight to the affected leg and slowly lower its heel only to the floor. drill_snapshot.evidence_notes: Fixed mechanics reviewed; sources: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/tendonitis/, https://myjointhealthhub.bnssg.nhs.uk/foot-ankle-pain/achilles-tendinopathy/, https://www.kentcht.nhs.uk/leaflet/achilles-insertional-tendinopathy/. Dormant LOAD content, not an active prescription. External load remains unknown where not measured. Tendon site, individual resistance, functional tolerance and a sourced evaluable transition are required before activation. Eccentrics are not assumed superior.

elbow_tendonitis.title: Supported hand-weight wrist extension
coaching_cues: Support the affected forearm palm-down on a table with the wrist free to move. With the hand empty, raise the wrist in the comfortable range, within any clinician restrictions, then slowly lower over five seconds. Keep the forearm supported. No dumbbell, band, forceful grip, forced end range, speed or automatic increase. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.
elbow_tendonitis.instructions: Support the affected forearm palm-down on a table with the wrist free to move. With the hand empty, raise the wrist in the comfortable range, within any clinician restrictions, then slowly lower over five seconds. Keep the forearm supported. No dumbbell, band, forceful grip, forced end range, speed or automatic increase. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.
stop_rules: Hand weight only: 1 set of 10, maximum once daily. No added resistance or automatic increase.
Keep the forearm supported and use only a comfortable range within clinician restrictions.
Stop for worsening during or delayed symptoms and seek clinical review.
Stop and seek assessment for trauma, loss of function, numbness, a hot red swollen elbow or fever.
Follow clinician restrictions; this grants no training or contact clearance.

drill_snapshot.name: Supported hand-weight wrist extension
drill_snapshot.notes: Support the affected forearm palm-down on a table with the wrist free to move. With the hand empty, raise the wrist in the comfortable range, within any clinician restrictions, then slowly lower over five seconds. Keep the forearm supported. No dumbbell, band, forceful grip, forced end range, speed or automatic increase. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.
target_tissues: common wrist extensor tendon at elbow
drill_snapshot.evidence_notes: Sources: https://www.rjah.nhs.uk/our-services/therapy/supported-self-care/tennis-elbow/ and https://www.jospt.org/doi/10.2519/jospt.2022.0302. Narrow hand-weight-only starter, not the dormant clinician-selected dumbbell candidate. For explicitly reported lateral tendon symptoms with rehabilitation loading permission and non-worsening reviewed RESTORE exposure. No grip strength or range-of-motion assessment is inferred. RJAH patient guidance supports the movement with symptom monitoring; the clinical guideline is not used to impose a consumer assessment checklist. Ten repetitions are the lower end of RJAH guidance; once-daily cap is a conservative product ceiling, not a universal clinical cadence or readiness threshold. No quantitative grip strength is inferred.

ankle_sprain.title: Seated controlled ankle heel raises
coaching_cues: Sit on a stable chair with both feet flat on the floor. Keeping the front of both feet on the floor, slowly raise both heels within a comfortable range and slowly lower them to the floor. Stay seated; no weights, band, pressure on the knees, step, forced range or automatic increase. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
ankle_sprain.instructions: Sit on a stable chair with both feet flat on the floor. Keeping the front of both feet on the floor, slowly raise both heels within a comfortable range and slowly lower them to the floor. Stay seated; no weights, band, pressure on the knees, step, forced range or automatic increase. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
stop_rules: Maximum 1 set of 10 once daily, seated with no added resistance or automatic increase.
Use only a comfortable range within clinician restrictions; stop for pain or worsening during or delayed symptoms.
Seek assessment for loss of function, inability to bear weight, bony tenderness, deformity, altered sensation, severe swelling or instability.
This grants no running, jumping, cutting, sparring or contact clearance.

drill_snapshot.name: Seated controlled ankle heel raises
drill_snapshot.notes: Sit on a stable chair with both feet flat on the floor. Keeping the front of both feet on the floor, slowly raise both heels within a comfortable range and slowly lower them to the floor. Stay seated; no weights, band, pressure on the knees, step, forced range or automatic increase. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
regress_when: Symptoms worsen: stop loading and follow conservative guidance.
stop_when: Stop for pain or worsening during or delayed symptoms. Follow clinician restrictions.
target_tissues: calf muscle-tendon unit acting at ankle
drill_snapshot.evidence_notes: OUH NHS ankle-sprain guidance supports seated heel raises with feet flat and slow lowering. Bexley NHS ankle-sprain guidance provides 10 repetitions in a comfortable range. One set, maximum once daily, no added resistance and mild clinician-described uncomplicated lateral presentation are conservative product limits, not validated LOAD thresholds or injury grades. This seated strengthening option does not certify standing weight-bearing tolerance, ROM, strength, stability or sport readiness. Existing RESTORE includes standing tasks; LOAD here is a bounded permission stage, not a claim this movement imposes greater force than every RESTORE task. Sources: https://www.jospt.org/doi/10.2519/jospt.2021.0302, https://www.ouh.nhs.uk/media/i0ldiecy/116454sprain.pdf, https://msk-bexley.nhs.uk/conditions/foot-and-ankle-pain/ankle-sprain, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8824326/

shoulder_tendonitis.title: Controlled wall push-ups
coaching_cues: Stand facing a stable wall, close enough to reach it comfortably without leaning. Place both hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder width, turned out slightly, with elbows below shoulders. Keep your body tall and feet fixed near the wall. Slowly bend your elbows a small comfortable amount to bring your body towards the wall, then gently push back. Keep within a pain-free range and clinician restrictions. Do not move your feet further back, lower your hands, add resistance or work to fatigue. Stop for pain, worsening symptoms during or after work, weakness or a feeling of instability.
shoulder_tendonitis.instructions: Stand facing a stable wall, close enough to reach it comfortably without leaning. Place both hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder width, turned out slightly, with elbows below shoulders. Keep your body tall and feet fixed near the wall. Slowly bend your elbows a small comfortable amount to bring your body towards the wall, then gently push back. Keep within a pain-free range and clinician restrictions. Do not move your feet further back, lower your hands, add resistance or work to fatigue. Stop for pain, worsening symptoms during or after work, weakness or a feeling of instability.
stop_rules: Stop for pain, worsening symptoms, weakness or instability during or after work.
Seek assessment for traumatic loss of function, suspected tear, altered sensation or unexplained weakness.

drill_snapshot.name: Controlled wall push-ups
drill_snapshot.notes: Stand facing a stable wall, close enough to reach it comfortably without leaning. Place both hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder width, turned out slightly, with elbows below shoulders. Keep your body tall and feet fixed near the wall. Slowly bend your elbows a small comfortable amount to bring your body towards the wall, then gently push back. Keep within a pain-free range and clinician restrictions. Do not move your feet further back, lower your hands, add resistance or work to fatigue. Stop for pain, worsening symptoms during or after work, weakness or a feeling of instability.
regress_when: Symptoms worsen: stop loading and follow conservative guidance.
stop_when: Stop for pain or worsening during or delayed symptoms. Follow clinician restrictions.
target_tissues: rotator cuff and shoulder girdle muscles
drill_snapshot.evidence_notes: 2025 rotator cuff tendinopathy CPG recommendation 25 supports active motor-control/resistance exercise with various loads, not a validated app LOAD threshold or one superior exercise. RJAH NHS describes wall push-ups with elbows below shoulders, 3 sets of 8; this option caps at 1 set of 8 at most once daily, feet near wall, small pain-free range, no foot-distance progression or added resistance. These are conservative product limits. Moderate is a conservative categorical upper-limb weight-bearing demand classification, not measured force or individual capacity. Bodyweight resistance varies with body position; it is not quantified. Only reported clinician-described non-traumatic cuff tendinopathy without tear and current rehabilitation loading permission apply; reported impact is not a clinical grade or measured capacity; this is not medical verification or measured strength/ROM. Sources: https://www.orthopt.org/uploads/content_files/files/Rotator_Cuff_CPG.pdf, https://www.rjah.nhs.uk/our-services/therapy/supported-self-care/rotator-cuff-related-shoulder-pain/ No numeric pain ceiling is inferred; the pain-free stop instruction is a conservative product restriction, not an unrestricted pain allowance.
